subject: Private deployment: evidence availability, escrow ask & MSA redlines
messages:
From: Michael Stroud <michael.stroud@acmehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tania Rojas <tania.rojas@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment requirements — escrow & evidence

Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with latency and the routing options. Procurement/legal have a few items we need to close before the SOW/Order Form can be signed for a private VPC deployment:  

- Confirmation of what you can provide as an escrow or custody mechanism for the model artifacts and inference binary in case Redwood is unavailable. We don't need pricing now, just the high-level triggers and access model.
- Audit scope: access to runtime audit logs, retention windows, and an example attestation for on-prem deployments.
- Evidence delivery timeline: sample runbook, brief test plan, and sample evidence artifacts (checksums, attestations).
- A redline to the MSA and Order Form reflecting deployment rights, license scope, and a mutually acceptable fallback (e.g., read-only images + signed attestation).

Can you confirm what you can share by next Tuesday (2027-04-13)? Also attaching the internal checklist they asked us to feed back on.

Best,
Michael
Procurement, Acme Health

Attachment: acme_vpc_checklist_20270408.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment requirements — escrow & evidence

Looping you in — Acme wants a concrete statement on an escrow/custody path, audit scope, and some redlines for the MSA/Order Form. They asked for delivery by Tue 4/13.

Marissa, can you pull the deployment runbook outline and the example evidence we usually share for on-prem customers (checksums, attestation template)?

Laura, can you propose narrow redlines that preserve our IP while satisfying their auditors (particularly around model custody triggers and access rights)? We want to avoid full source deposit if possible — thinking: signed snapshot + HSM escrow + contingent retrieval process.

I'll coordinate with Karthik for deal language/thresholds.

Thanks — Grace
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_vpc_checklist_20270408.xlsx (forwarded)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment requirements — escrow & evidence

Grace / Laura — attaching our runbook outline and an evidence matrix we use for private deployments. Highlights:

- Evidence matrix rows: environment prep, image checksums, service attestation, KV cache purge, network isolation checks.
- Delivery estimate: sample artifacts (checksums + attestations) can be provided within 5 business days after Order Form signature.
- Escrow candidate: we can provide an encrypted unexecutable artifact plus an HSM-wrapped key escrow held by third-party custodian; retrieval requires joint attestation and pre-agreed triggers (company insolvency, sustained failure to respond >90 days, or material breach of SLA).

I'm comfortable with that approach as a starting point. Attached: deployment_runbook_outline.pdf and evidence_matrix_ACME.xlsx.

Marissa
Principal PM, Customer Deployments

Attachments: deployment_runbook_outline.pdf; evidence_matrix_ACME.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment requirements — escrow & evidence

Folks — I drafted narrow redlines that address: custody triggers, limited deposit scope (artifact+decryption key, not source), audit access (read-only logs, redact PII), and attestation procedures. Key points:

- Deposit mechanics: third-party custodian (we propose IronLock) holds a AES-wrapped key and encrypted artifact. Retrieval requires (a) written certification by Acme's GC + a court order OR (b) sustained Redwood failure >90 days with demonstrable remediation attempts.
- License scope: customer receives a runtime license limited to the deployed environment and cannot extract model weights without joint retrieval.
- Audit rights: we will provide exportable, time-limited log snapshots and an annual attestation. On-site audits are permitted with 30 days notice and reasonable confidentiality protections.
- Indemnity/limitations: keep standard liability caps; avoid any warranty about model output for regulated decisions.

I attached redlines in both PDF and Word for comments. If Acme insists on broader custody we should discuss commercial concessions (extended warranty credits or discounted on-prem professional hours).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_MSA_v1.pdf; redlines_OrderForm_v1.docx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Michael Stroud <michael.stroud@acmehealth.com>, Tania Rojas <tania.rojas@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed path for escrow & evidence (attachments)

Michael / Tania — thanks for the clear ask. Sharing our proposed path and narrow redlines (attached) so you can review with legal. Summary:

1) Escrow approach: encrypted runtime artifact + HSM-key with a third-party custodian (IronLock). Triggers limited to insolvency, court order, or 90-day sustained failure to maintain SLA after remediation steps.
2) Evidence & runbooks: sample runbook and evidence matrix attached. We can provide sample checksums, attestation templates, and a staging test plan within 5 business days post-signature.
3) Audit access: exportable read-only logs (redacted), annual attestation, and limited on-site audit with NDA/filters.
4) Commercial path: If Acme requires unconditional deposit or immediate retrieval rights, we'll need to discuss a commercial concession (one-time escrow fee or extended support credit).

Please see the attached redlines_MSA_v1.pdf and the Order Form redlines in Word. Happy to set a 30-min sync today or tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_MSA_v1.pdf; redlines_OrderForm_v1.docx

From: Tania Rojas <tania.rojas@acmehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Michael Stroud <michael.stroud@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed path for escrow & evidence (attachments)

Grace / team — thanks, helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our legal team after a first pass: 

- Can you confirm the exact retention window for logs and whether logs will include request-level metadata (timestamps, route, token counts) or be limited to service-level telemetry?
- For the 90-day trigger, can you provide a short SLA exception process (who logs the incident, remediation steps, and evidence that remediation was attempted)? We need that language to feed into our SOC review.
- On the escrow custodian: would Redwood accept a different custodian if Acme's compliance team prefers (Acme can propose)?

If you can answer those three items and we can get a short updated MSA snippet, we can escalate to GC and try to sign the Order Form this week.

Thanks — Tania
Head of Vendor Risk, Acme Health

Quoted earlier: "We can provide an encrypted unexecutable artifact plus an HSM-wrapped key escrow held by third-party custodian; retrieval requires joint attestation and pre-agreed triggers (company insolvency, sustained failure to respond >90 days, or material breach of SLA)."

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Tania Rojas <tania.rojas@acmehealth.com>, Michael Stroud <michael.stroud@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed path for escrow & evidence (attachments)

Tania — answers inline below and next steps: 

- Logs: we will provide exportable, redacted request logs that include timestamp, route ID, and token counts (no PII payloads). Retention window: 12 months by default; we can extend to 24 months with a contractual addendum.

- SLA exception process / 90-day trigger: we will propose MSA language that requires (a) incident logged via Redwood support portal with ticket ID, (b) 30-day remediation period with weekly status updates, (c) 60-day escalation to an executive review, and (d) 90-day declaration of persistent unavailability if no remediation achieved. Retrieval from escrow requires Acme's written request + either a court order or the declaration described. I'll have Laura add a short procedural clause to the redlines.

- Custodian: yes — Redwood is open to customer-proposed custodians subject to standard onboarding checks. We'll include a line that allows mutual approval of the custodian.

Next steps: Laura will publish a short MSA redline snippet reflecting the log retention, the SLA exception steps, and the custodian approval clause by EOD tomorrow. Marissa will prepare the sample evidence bundle to share once the Order Form is countersigned. Karthik / I will coordinate any commercial concessions if Acme requests unconditional retrieval.

Can we do a 20-min call tomorrow 10:00am PT to align? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Grace
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
